titleText.es: Los contenidos de cualquier viñeta son dependientes de los contenidos de todas las viñetas incluyendo a ella misma. El grafo de las dependencias entre viñetas es completo y bidireccional, y cada nodo tiene un ciclo. Este texto tiene doscientos setenta y tres caracteres.
titleText.en: The contents of any one panel are dependent on the contents of every panel including itself. The graph of panel dependencies is complete and bidirectional, and each node has a loop. The mouseover text has two hundred and forty-two characters.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish text is the exact title attribute in the Spanish archive; the English text is the exact official xkcd title attribute, whose stated character count intentionally differs.

cards.promptEs: porción · cantidad · posición · viñetas dentro de la imagen
cards.answerEn: each panel measures the same image, and the position panel contains smaller copies of all three panels
cards.noteEn: The strip is self-describing: one panel labels the white and black portions, another graphs black ink by panel, and the last plots where that ink appears. Because the final plot contains thumbnails of the panels, its own content contributes recursively to the quantities and positions it depicts.

cards.promptEs: adjetivo que concuerda con masculino o femenino
cards.questionEn: How does a Spanish describing word change for a man, woman, or gendered noun?
cards.answerEn: Make the describing word match the gender and number of the person or thing it describes.
cards.noteEn: Many describing words ending in -o change to -a for a feminine singular person or noun: cansado becomes cansada. Plurals normally add -s. Some describing words have one form for both genders.

example.es: Pedro está cansado y Ana está cansada.
example.en: Pedro is tired and Ana is tired.

cards.noteEn: Que connects a noun to information describing it. Depending on the noun, English translates it as “who,” “that,” or “which.”

example.es: La persona que llamó es mi amiga.
example.en: The person who called is my friend.

cards.answerEn: of; or no separate English word, linking an amount to what it measures
cards.noteEn: After a quantity expression, de introduces the substance or thing being measured. English uses “of” in expressions such as a lot of or the amount of, but may leave de untranslated in others, such as un poco de agua, “a little water.”

cards.questionEn: Where does a basic Spanish describing word usually go relative to its noun?
cards.answerEn: Put it after the noun in the common neutral order.
cards.noteEn: Many ordinary descriptive words follow the person or thing they describe: un coche rojo, una casa grande. Some adjectives commonly come before the noun, and moving an adjective can change emphasis or meaning, so this is a useful default rather than an absolute rule.
Por can introduce the unit used to divide or distribute a quantity. The unit after por stays singular when it means “for each one.”

example.en: There are two books per student.

cards.noteEn: Viñeta can also mean a small illustration or vignette. As a comics term, it names one framed panel of a comic strip.

example.es: La primera viñeta no tiene diálogo.
example.en: The first comic panel has no dialogue.
